comparisons.reason: Both are argument-only binary measures of OP's own central claim certainty with the same null rule, but the rubrics differ. Feature 0 returns 1 when the main thesis is mainly framed with high-modality or certainty markers. It tolerates some hedging, and it covers 'must' and 'clearly'. It excludes marked edits. Feature 1 requires an absolute, unqualified declarative and returns 1 only if the argument has no hedging or qualifying language about the main claim. A thesis with strong markers plus a qualifier would be 1 under feature 0 and 0 under feature 1. Feature 1 does not mention excluding edits. Feature 1 also does not allow high modality without absoluteness. An explicit decision on hedging tolerance and edit handling is pending. Both rubrics are kept as written.
